name: Tulsi Gabbard
role: US Director of National Intelligence (2025-2026); former Democratic US Representative from Hawaii (2013-2021)
summary: Gabbard is a military veteran whose signature position is opposition to regime-change wars and presidential war-making without Congress, paired with civil-liberties stances on surveillance and encryption. She moved from the Democratic left (Medicare for All, an assault-weapons ban, climate legislation) to independent in 2022 and Republican in 2024, criticising the Democratic Party over wokeness, borders, and foreign policy, and served in the Trump administration.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Cosponsored the Expanded & Improved Medicare for All Act (2017) and a later single-payer bill that allows private insurance (2019); in the July 2019 debate she called the US a 'sick care system' and said many cannot afford care. No later reversal found.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Supported a bill raising the federal minimum wage to $15 by 2024; a 2019 questionnaire summary lists the same $15 position. Support is shown by bill backing, not extended statements.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Her Medicare for All plan was to be partly funded by taxing the wealthy and financial transactions (2017); a 2019 summary lists taxing the wealthiest 5%. These date from her Democratic years and her later view is not documented.

unions-good.rationale: She praises Hawaiian union organizing for overcoming plantation abuses and giving workers an effective voice.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Record of backing tighter finance and tech rules: called for breaking up big banks (2012), cosponsored restoring Glass-Steagall (2017), introduced the Wall Street Banker Accountability for Misconduct Act (2019) and called for breaking up big tech.

cut-welfare.rationale: She calls for preserving and strengthening Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Points both ways: opposed bulk data collection (2014) and calls herself a strong civil libertarian (2026), but as DNI nominee called FISA 702 'essential for our national security' while saying it must sit alongside civil-liberties safeguards.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Supports legalising recreational marijuana (introduced the Ending Federal Marijuana Prohibition Act and backed the MORE Act) and called the drug war a failure; no recorded view on other recreational drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: She explicitly opposes criminalizing abhorrent speech protected by the First Amendment.

limit-guns.rationale: Supported an assault-weapons ban and universal background checks as a Democrat (2019), but later stated opposition to an assault weapons ban (Oct 2024) and supports the Second Amendment and the Bruen ruling, so the later position is the weaker-regulation one.

empower-police-military.rationale: Criticised 'defund the police' as demonizing law enforcement and, in her 2022 party-exit statement, accused Democrats of demonizing police; in 2019 she opposed cutting the military budget. Neither is an explicit call for more funding and authority.

traditional-family.rationale: She describes family as the foundational fabric of civilization.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Early career opposed same-sex marriage (supported her father's 2004 campaign for a Hawaii amendment; 2002 support for a marriage amendment), apologised in 2012 and 2019, later signed an amicus brief supporting the challenge to DOMA and joined the LGBT Equality Caucus. Current view is support for legal marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: In 2019 she said abortion should remain legal and accessible and set the limit at the third trimester (life or severe health risk excepted); in Dec 2020 she introduced a bill to bar abortions after 20 weeks. Reported to have moved toward the Republican position since 2022, but no clear updated statement was found.

more-religion-public.rationale: She opposes removing God from public life and defends freely expressed public faith, including atheists’ equal freedom.

reduce-immigration.rationale: No recorded position found on overall immigration levels.

free-trade.rationale: Opposed the TPP and said she backs 'fair trade, not trade deals that give away the sovereignty of the American people' and jobs (2019 debate). She did not oppose trade as such.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Calls herself a 'dove' on regime-change wars, said there are very few examples of wars justifying US force (citing World War II) and opposed intervention in Syria and Libya-style change efforts. She did not address human-rights interventions by name.

open-borders.rationale: In her Oct 2022 statement leaving the party she criticised Democrats because they 'believe in open borders'; in 2019 she backed 'secure borders as well as humane immigration policies'.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Introduced the Off Fossil Fuels Act (100% clean electricity by 2035, fracking ban) and in the 2019 debate called it the most ambitious climate bill in Congress. Reported to have shifted on environment after 2022 without a documented new statement.

expand-nuclear.rationale: In Feb 2019 she said she did not support 'leaving the door open' to nuclear power until there is a permanent waste solution. Later view not documented.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In the 2019 debate she said Trump's tariff approach was 'extremely volatile without any clear strategic plan' and hurt manufacturers and farmers, and she would not keep it.

democracy-best.rationale: She defends voters’ freedom to choose even when elites believe their choice would be wrong.

separate-church-state.rationale: She explicitly defends constitutional separation and rejects governments imposing religious morality.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: She rejects government imposing personal religious morality through law, while protecting individual belief.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: As a member of Congress she introduced a bill barring mandates for encryption bypass; at the 2025 hearing she reaffirmed: 'These back doors lead down a dangerous path that can undermine Americans' Fourth Amendment rights and civil liberties.'

results-over-ideology.rationale: Her questionnaire emphasizes delivering results by working across ideological and party disagreements.

total-state.rationale: At Dartmouth she rejects a state directing housing, food and every aspect of people’s lives.

economic-freedom.rationale: Her Dartmouth argument says state provision without control over one’s economic choices is not freedom.

reason-over-faith.rationale: She explicitly presents faith and spiritual practice as guides to her decisions and service.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The Off Fossil Fuels Act she introduced would end fossil electricity and ban fracking (2017, 2019); no recent statement on production.

national-mission.rationale: Opposed 'neolibs and neocons' who promote regime change (Feb 2019 launch) and called for ending 'wasteful regime change wars'.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Said in the 2019 debate that Trump won because people felt left behind by 'self serving politicians on both sides', and in 2022 described Democratic leaders as an 'elitist cabal of warmongers'.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said she would fight for 'justice and equality for all' and every American 'regardless of race or religion' (2019 debate opening).

consent-of-governed.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

separated-powers.rationale: Her war-powers work (No More Presidential Wars Act, Soleimani and Syria measures) argues Congress must check the president, and she called the Soleimani strike unconstitutional; this is about war powers only.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Written answer 184 insists due process and judicial oversight still apply to citizen enemy-combatant detention.

party-controls-media.rationale: Compared the Disinformation Governance Board to the Ministry of Truth (2026 remarks), criticised platform bans of users and said free speech is under pressure; opposes government deciding what is true.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Objected that the TPP 'gave away our sovereignty to a panel of international corporations' (2019 debate). This concerns a trade tribunal, not the EU model.

death-penalty.rationale: A 2019 questionnaire summary lists her as backing abolition of capital punishment; no later statement found and the source is an aggregator.

religious-exemptions.rationale: She expressly supports religious accommodation for minority faiths in different institutional settings.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

women-must-cover.rationale: She describes compulsory burqas under theocracies as oppressive state control of women.

ban-cartels.rationale: Called for breaking up big banks (2012) and big tech, cosponsored restoring Glass-Steagall; no explicit cartel statement.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Criticised the TPP for lacking clear protections for the environment and for costing jobs, and called for fair trade deals that protect both (2019 debate).

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: She says constitutional rights must constrain whoever holds power, protecting even political enemies.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Introduced H.R. 4108 (2015) to end US efforts to overthrow Assad and bar funds for Syrian opposition groups; the Stop Arming Terrorists Act became law via the FY2020 NDAA. In 2022 she called the Ukraine conflict a US-NATO regime-change war by proxy.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said big insurance and big pharma have 'had a seat at the table, writing this legislation' (2019 debate); pledged to take no corporate PAC money and cosponsored the We the People Amendment to abolish corporate personhood.

non-intervention.rationale: Strong opposition to regime-change wars and arguing against intervention in Syria and Venezuela, but she also supported UN investigation and ICC prosecution of Assad if found responsible and backs force against terrorists, so the absolute wording does not fit.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Opposed the TPP because rulings of an international panel 'would supersede any domestic law', calling that 'extremely dangerous' (2019 debate). Applies to trade tribunals specifically.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Mixed: member of the LGBT Equality Caucus and high HRC score earlier, but in 2020 introduced a bill limiting girls' school sports to those assigned female at birth and endorsed Florida's parental-rights law (2022). No statement on legal recognition itself.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Distinguished Islamism, which she called the ideology behind ISIS and al-Qaeda, from Islam (2016); in 2025 she warned of 'Islamist ideology'. She frames the problem as Islamism, not Islam.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Served in the military for over two decades, calls herself a hawk against terrorists, and in 2019 said not to cut the military budget; no statement on abolition itself.

racial-franchise.rationale: She rejects judging eligibility for public office by race or religion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Criticised the 'defund the police' movement and in 2022 said Democrats 'demonize the police and protect criminals'.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Her campaigns centred on warning of nuclear catastrophe ('a new Cold War... brink of nuclear catastrophe', 2019; Democrats 'dragging us ever closer to nuclear war', 2022), but she has not framed it as extinction-risk policy.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Cosponsored recognition of the Armenian Genocide (2019).

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: She explicitly calls biological differences between men and women objective truths.

spiritual-nature.rationale: She describes public service as caring for God’s children, grounded in spiritual purpose.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Opposes regime-change wars and said very few wars justify force, but she enlisted to go after al-Qaeda after 9/11 and supports counter-terror operations abroad.

free-public-college.rationale: Supported free community college for all and free four-year college for families earning up to $125,000, funded by a stock and bond trade tax.

arms-reduction.rationale: She urges renewed US-Russian-Chinese negotiations to reduce nuclear arsenals and end the arms race.

student-debt-relief.rationale: In the 2019 debate she called student debt crushing and called for 'bold, creative solutions' and investments. No specific cancellation proposal found.

religions-one-truth.rationale: She says one God has many names and authentic faiths share eternal principles of love and service.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Written answer 162 qualifies her repeal proposal with conditional emergency powers, oversight and protection of essential networks.

women-suffrage.rationale: Her argument rejects gender-based tests for office, and her 2026 address encourages women’s political leadership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: In April 2017 she said she supported ICC prosecution of Assad if he was found responsible for chemical attacks. Conditional.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: She condemns religious tests and choosing officeholders for or against their faith.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Proposed funding Medicare for All and free college partly by taxing financial transactions (stock and bond trades), which is close to but not the currency-trade tax in the statement.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Said real patriotism means 'serving the interest of all Americans, not just the rich and powerful' (2019 debate opening).

material-over-identity.rationale: In 2022 she said Democrats divide people by 'racializing every issue' and 'cowardly wokeness', and in 2019 argued people were left behind and resources should go to needs at home. No direct statement on the left's focus.

notes:
Views shifted markedly: early anti-same-sex-marriage activism (apologised 2012, 2019); Democratic positions to 2020 on healthcare, guns, climate; since 2022 more conservative on guns, abortion limits, and transgender sports, per reporting, though many later positions were not documented in sources opened. On FISA 702 she called for repeal in Congress but described it as essential at her 2025 hearing, supporting a warrant requirement for US-person queries with exigent exceptions; she said Snowden broke the law and she would no longer advocate a pardon. Role end date: she resigned as DNI in June 2026 (Dartmouth report says June; Wikipedia gives effective June 2026). Not accessible: congress.gov, the Senate Intelligence Committee PDFs (including written answers), govtrack, and the full text of her book.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 27 answers taken from it, 17 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent third-model pass; all active statements and the full blank list reviewed. No previous answer values were read. Only separate-church-state among the ten prioritized items has an exact documented political position. Hindu identity, eternal-soul belief and descriptions of political corruption do not establish divine political sovereignty, religion-as-illusion, Marxist doctrines or revolutionary strategy. No living-person inferences. The newly recovered Senate written answers were OCRed from the official scan, with printed page numbers retained. Senators’ questions are not treated as her commitments. Her lawful conditional surveillance position is distinguished from blanket acceptance of domestic tracking, which she criticized in October 2026. Current opposition to encryption backdoors is explicit in oral testimony. Her abortion answer favors state jurisdiction but specifies no gestational limit: numbers in the preceding discussion belong to hosts and a Trump clip. Abortion is low-confidence mixed because her current substantive legal standard remains unclear, rather than being inferred from Republican affiliation. Sex-based sports rules and childhood-transition criticism do not establish a comprehensive position on adult legal gender recognition; that item stays null. Older healthcare and climate commitments have no explicit later repudiation in the examined material; endorsements of Trump do not transfer his policies to her. Likewise, service in his administration does not cancel her stated dissent over the 2026 Iran war. Her review of intelligence and official secrecy is not a general commitment to public access to all government records. Anti-regime-change arguments do not establish the absolute non-intervention statement, abolition of armed forces or rejection of every military alliance. Gun rights as a check on tyranny do not expressly endorse revolution. Religious freedom does not establish specific apostasy, conversion, blasphemy or public-school curriculum policies. No generic all-drug legalization position is extrapolated from cannabis reform. No negative positions are assigned simply from missing evidence. All rhetoric remains medium or low confidence.
